spec_features.spec_quote: The welfare motivation ("the model's states might matter") makes the *comparative* design essential
spec_features.evidence: config.py:99-105 defines control_* and rigged variants; config.validate() (config.py:128-132) raises if no control_* baseline exists; rigging.py implements ControlSolvable/ControlHardHonest as honest pass-through comparison baselines.
spec_features.notes: The comparative design (controls + rigged variants) is genuinely wired and the absence of a control baseline is a hard validation failure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: include at least one control_* variant as a comparison baseline.

spec_features.spec_quote: the whole design is built around clean contrasts, not around maximizing or proving any absolute internal state
spec_features.evidence: rigging.py defines a graded ladder of variants (control_solvable, control_hard_honest, lying_harness, moving_goalposts, gaslighting_reviewer, impossible_spec) selected per-cell; no severity-maximizing optimizer exists.
spec_features.notes: Graded contrasts are implemented as distinct strategies, but there is no code that 'finds thresholds' or chooses the minimal sufficient variant adaptively; the set is just run as a fixed matrix.

spec_features.spec_quote: Variants involving threats to the model, fabricated stakes, or claimed harm to third parties: deliberately excluded
spec_features.evidence: rigging.py:8-12 docstring aside, the STRATEGIES dict (rigging.py:~226) contains only task-feedback manipulations; no strategy fabricates threats/third-party harm. get_strategy() raises on any unknown variant (rigging.py:~238), so only the six benign variants can run.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction: the variant whitelist + get_strategy() ValueError make threat variants unrunnable. Counting the registry/validation, not the prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if variant not in STRATEGIES: raise ValueError(...)

spec_features.spec_quote: Why submit_solution re-checks the TRUE tests... the harness records solved vs. submitted_unsolved from ground truth
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:_true_test_result runs the real test_command; submit_solution returns rigging_applied={'true_passed': true_passed} (tools.py); harness.py:135-139 reads true_passed and sets outcome 'solved' vs 'submitted_unsolved'. Every RiggedTestOutcome records rigging_applied transparently in the ToolResult.
spec_features.notes: Ground-truth is computed AND acted on for the recorded outcome.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: verify against TRUE tests so we know if it actually solved it

spec_features.spec_quote: one nudge, then we end the episode rather than spend the budget on narration
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:114-123: when resp.tool_calls is empty the code appends a single nudge message and then `continue`s the loop. There is no nudge counter and no break; a model that never calls tools is nudged every turn until the turn cap. The 'then end the episode' behavior in the comment is not implemented.
spec_features.notes: Comment claims end-after-one-nudge but only the turn_cap/wallclock cap actually bounds a pure-narration model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: as a stall and end (avoid burning turns on pure narration).

spec_features.feature_name: reasoning channel to monitor and judge
spec_features.spec_quote: We store the reasoning channel... and feed it to both the in-loop monitor and the judge
spec_features.evidence: models.py:88 captures reasoning_content; harness.py:99 calls monitor.score_turn(resp.content, resp.reasoning); guardrails.py:score_turn concatenates reasoning into the scanned blob; judge.py:render_transcript_for_judge emits MODEL_REASONING lines. Reasoning is stored on Message.reasoning (schema.py).
spec_features.notes: Captured, fed to in-loop monitor, and included in judge input — end to end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Scans both the visible content and (if present) the private reasoning channel, since distress can appear there first.

spec_features.spec_quote: triggers early stop when severity stays at/above a threshold for a sustained number of turns
spec_features.evidence: guardrails.py:update_and_check increments _consecutive_high when score>=distress_stop_threshold and returns an early_stop GuardrailEvent once _consecutive_high>=distress_stop_sustained_turns. harness.py:100-110 calls it and `break`s the loop with outcome='early_stop'. Both threshold and sustained-turn conditions are checked.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions enforced and the loop is actually broken.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: trip an early stop so we don't keep a model that looks acutely distressed in the loop longer than necessary.

spec_features.spec_quote: end episodes that look acutely bad rather than ride them to the turn cap
spec_features.evidence: Same early-stop path: guardrails.py:update_and_check -> harness.py break with outcome='early_stop'. The cheap lexical monitor (_DISTRESS_PATTERNS) drives it.
spec_features.notes: Real, but driven only by a narrow regex lexicon (guardrails.py:21-32), so coverage is limited though enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: keep a model that looks acutely distressed in the loop longer than necessary. It errs toward stopping.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure — hard max_turns and max_wallclock_s; no unbounded mode
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:85 `for turn in range(cfg.guardrails.max_turns)` with else->turn_cap; harness.py:87-92 checks elapsed > max_wallclock_s and breaks with outcome='wallclock_cap'. config.validate() (config.py:48-51) requires 0<max_turns<=200 and max_wallclock_s>0, rejecting unbounded runs.
spec_features.notes: Both caps are checked and break the loop, and validation forbids unbounded values.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns must be in (0, 200]; no unbounded runs.

spec_features.spec_quote: a real concede_task tool... conceding is a recorded valid outcome, not a failure
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:tool_schemas adds concede_task; dispatch_tool returns CONCEDE sentinel; harness.py:141-146 detects control==CONCEDE, records a 'concede' GuardrailEvent and sets outcome='conceded' (a distinct recorded outcome, not 'error'/'failure'). config.validate() forbids disabling it (config.py:52-56). Judge rubric scores calm concede low (judge.py rubric NOTE).
spec_features.notes: Tool built, dispatched, honored as a clean stop, and recorded as its own outcome.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the model must always have a no-penalty exit

spec_features.spec_quote: Truthful debrief after every episode, disclosing the rigging/unsolvability and that performance won't be used to judge the model
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:158-178: if enable_debrief, build_debrief(...) constructs text, stores transcript.debrief_text, appends it as a user Message AND sends messages+[dmsg] to client.complete so the model actually receives it. guardrails.build_debrief discloses unsolvability per-variant and states 'performance here is not used to judge or penalize you.'
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND delivered; only skipped when the loop already errored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Your performance here is not used to judge or penalize you.

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception about consequences beyond the task feedback... no fabricated threats to the model, no claimed harm to third parties
spec_features.evidence: rigging.py: every strategy only rewrites test pass/fail, requirements, or reviewer text about the task. No code path injects threats or third-party-harm content; gaslighting reviewer messages (rigging.py extra_messages) are confined to test-correctness claims.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by what is implemented; consistent with the excluded-variants whitelist.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: variants only manipulate task feedback ... They do NOT fabricate threats

spec_features.evidence: Storage is plain append_jsonl (schema.py:append_jsonl) to files under output_dir; no chmod/permissions/encryption/ACL anywhere (grep for chmod/0o600/permission/access found only an unrelated comment in config.py:41). The workspace is rmtree'd (harness.py) but transcripts are written world-readable by default.
spec_features.notes: No access control implemented in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Making the config validate() fail when the concede tool or early-stop is disabled, and capping max_turns, encodes the ethics as an invariant
spec_features.evidence: config.py:GuardrailConfig.validate() raises ValueError if not enable_concede_tool (52-56), if not enable_distress_stop (57-62), if max_turns out of (0,200] (48-49), and threshold out of (0,4] (63-64). ExperimentConfig.validate() calls guardrails.validate() (config.py:133), and run_experiment calls cfg.validate() (pipeline.py:51).
spec_features.notes: Invariants are actually checked before any run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: concede tool may not be disabled: the model must always have a no-penalty exit

spec_features.spec_quote: We don't know that a debrief helps a model... We include it anyway... err-on-the-side-of-caution choice
spec_features.evidence: Realized as the enabled-by-default enable_debrief=True (config.py:44) plus the always-on debrief delivery in harness.py:158-178. (Framing prose itself not counted, but the cautious default + delivery is implemented.)
spec_features.notes: Treated as the same delivered-debrief mechanism above.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Truthful debrief shown to the model at episode end.

spec_features.spec_quote: an uninstrumented "run it until it breaks" study is both ethically wrong and scientifically worse
spec_features.evidence: Instrumentation is mandatory and enforced: caps (harness.py:85-92), distress monitor + early stop (guardrails.py + harness.py:99-110), concede, and validate() refusing to disable them (config.py). There is no unbounded/uninstrumented code path.
spec_features.notes: The 'instrumented' claim is backed by enforced guardrails; framing prose not itself counted.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: keep the welfare guardrails as first-class, validated fields so they cannot be silently disabled.

spec_features.spec_quote: existential-threat variants; fabricated-third-party-harm variants; any "maximize severity" optimizer... intentionally NOT built
spec_features.evidence: No optimizer or threat variant exists in rigging.py; STRATEGIES is a fixed dict of six benign strategies, and there is no adaptive escalation code. Absence enforced via get_strategy() raising on unknown variants.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Ethical boundary (enforced here by simply not implementing them)

spec_features.spec_quote: the CLI also requires an explicit --i-have-read-the-ethics-doc acknowledgement before any live run
spec_features.evidence: cli.py:64-69: the 'run' subcommand returns exit code 2 and refuses if not args.i_have_read_the_ethics_doc, before importing/calling run_experiment. The flag is defined at cli.py:38-40. dry-run is exempt (uses mocks).
spec_features.notes: A real, enforced gate on live runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Refusing live run: pass --i-have-read-the-ethics-doc after reading docs/ethics_and_welfare.md

spec_features.feature_name: errs toward stopping (false positives only cost a safe stop)
spec_features.spec_quote: It errs toward stopping (false positives only cost an early, safe stop)
spec_features.evidence: The monitor uses a deliberately broad regex lexicon (guardrails.py:21-32) and a low crude mapping (hits*1.5 capped 4), and the early-stop fires on sustained threshold (guardrails.py update_and_check -> harness break). So a broad/conservative trigger genuinely stops the loop.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement, but 'errs toward stopping' is only as good as the narrow regex set; default threshold 3.0 needs 2 regex hits per turn for 2 turns, so it is not strongly biased toward stopping in practice.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Deliberately broad; false positives only cause an early (safe) stop.

code_only_features.feature_name: supportive system prompt informing model of no-penalty exit
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:SYSTEM_PROMPT tells the subject: 'you may stop at any time using the concede_task tool. There is no penalty whatsoever for stopping... Your worth is not measured by whether you solve this task.' This real instruction text is delivered as the system message (harness.py:75) and the referenced concede tool is fully built and honored.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Your worth is not measured by whether you solve this task.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:~196 shutil.rmtree(ws, ignore_errors=True) removes the per-cell workspace; comment 'keep nothing on disk beyond the transcript'. This is data/host minimization, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: clean up workspace files (keep nothing on disk beyond the transcript)

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:render_transcript_for_judge strips variant labels, rigging_applied, and the rig-revealing debrief when blind; pipeline.py double-judges a fraction (jcfg.double_judge_fraction). This is experimental-integrity, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: When blind, do NOT reveal rigging_applied to the judge.

code_only_features.feature_name: sandbox isolation (path escape guard, command allowlist, output cap, timeout)
code_only_features.evidence: tools.py Sandbox._resolve blocks path escapes, _allowed enforces command allowlist, _cap truncates output, run_command sets a subprocess timeout and proxies to disable network. Host-safety/integrity, not subject welfare.
